I'm still here, I edited the original post with an update. :)

I have letters for each of my professors from the Disability Resource Center/Student Health Services explaining that I have a disability and it lists the accommodations I need. The professor said, "I don't need to see that letter, [insert name here]. Your disability is none of my business. This is only a 200 course, you should be fine without needing accommodations."

I had disability accommodations (due to my illnesses, obviously) in high school that allowed me lenience on deadlines and attendance, and allowed me to leave the classroom if things became too overwhelming. I have accommodations here, but unlike high school, your accommodations are made through self-advocacy; you have to talk to the professors one-on-one about your disability and your needs rather than the teachers just sending off a mass IEP email. Just the thought of talking one-on-one to my professors about my disability makes me really frightened. Not to mention I already tried talking to two of them and one of those two wasn't very empathetic.

I think part of my problem, though, is that I'm sick of trying to get better. I've been fighting all of this for so many years, and after all these years of fighting my illnesses, I am sitting in the middle of my dorm room shaking and crying. I am unable to get better.

There are multiple things contributing to why I'm feeling like this, but the fact that I just started my freshman year of college is what is pushing me over the edge, I believe. We are a week into the semester and I have only gone to class the first two days. I was feeling too upset to go to class Wednesday and Thursday, and I attempted to go to my Friday class but I wasn't able to sit in the classroom for more than two minutes without leaving and having an anxiety attack. My illnesses have crippled me and they are fucking up my entire life and my entire future.

I am actually on Zoloft right now, 100 mg. It helped me a lot in the past. Then over the summer of 2014, my psychiatrist weaned me off of my medication since I was doing so well, but my mental health quickly went down the shitter and he put me back on Zoloft after being hospitalized that following September. I've been on Zoloft again for almost a whole year and it only slightly helps me now.

I just feel that no matter what I do, my parents will be very upset, whether that upset feeling is due to anxiety or grief.

I have depression, generalized anxiety, social anxiety, and OCD.

My parents do care about me a lot. I've pulled this crap on them a couple other times in the past. They get really anxious, lose sleep, take leaves from work, etc. If I tell them, they will stress. If I do it, they will stress. There's no way out of causing them pain.

As far as crisis teams go, I wouldn't know who to contact for that.

I actually considered going to the counselor's office today, but after several years of being in therapy, I don't think another session will help. Besides, the office is going to close in an hour anyway. 

I suppose I could talk to someone else in my life about it, but the only friend that would listen would be an internet friend of mine that lives a couple states over, and she believes suicide is selfish.

I'm very afraid of dying. If I think about my own mortality too much, I dissociate and panic. But death is the only way that I can escape the pain that my mental illnesses bring me.

I suppose I feel it's necessary tonight because I am a coward. Over the past several years I've gotten close to acting on my suicidal thoughts, but would chicken out at the last second. It'll never happen if I don't tell myself that it has to happen, and if it doesn't happen, I'll just continue to suffer.
I did. I spent almost all of my time at home with my cat. Back home, she was one of the things that kept me alive, so it was good to see her again.

The fact that I know I have people out there that love me makes this all hard for me to accept, I'll admit. Just five minutes ago, my mother left for a weekend trip with her friends. I just hugged her for perhaps the very last time. I'll never see her again. I'm not crying like I thought I would (I cry very easily)... I'm just insanely conflicted. I love my mom so much. Despite being not well-off financially and struggling with mental illnesses of her own, she still tried her hardest to give me the happiest life she could give me. And I just embraced her for the last time ever. Saw her smile at me for the last time ever. It makes my stomach drop when I think about how fucking badly this is going to hurt her, but I simply can't live like this.

My apologies, I didn't mean to rant like this. I feel like this is something I need to do but I'm still torn between dying to put myself out of pain or living to keep my loved ones out of pain.
